evidence_quotes: 39 seismic events of magnitude 5.0 or greater were recorded globally between 2026-01-17 and 2026-02-16
Tobelo, Indonesia led all regions with 6 events, followed by La Tirana, Chile and the Mariana Islands region, each with 4 events
maximum magnitude of 6.2 recorded at Nikolski, Alaska

Three events in the sample dataset were flagged tsunami: true — the magnitude 5.7 at 55 km E of Kermadec Islands (depth 5.7 km, 2026-02-08), the magnitude 5.5 in the New Britain region, PNG (depth 7.4 km, 2026-02-03), and the magnitude 5.5 at 30 km E of Tual, Indonesia (depth 5.4 km, 2026-01-27)
two magnitude 6.1 earthquakes (2026-01-30 at 96.9 km depth and 2026-02-02 at 184.2 km depth)
the sample events section contains 30 of the 39 total events; full event-level details for the remaining 9 events are not derivable from current data
criticisms: The report states the two M6.1 La Tirana events occurred 'in a 3-day window (2026-01-30 to 2026-02-02)' — this is actually a 3-day span which is accurate, but the framing is slightly misleading since the digest shows these are on Jan 30 and Feb 2, which is technically a 3-day gap. This is a minor phrasing issue, not a factual error.

The report claims 'events under 30 km depth in this region have previously been associated with tsunami flags elsewhere in the digest' when referring to Tobelo — this is an inferential leap not directly supported by the digest data, though it is framed cautiously enough ('have previously been associated') to be acceptable as analytical commentary rather than a fabricated fact.
The report correctly counts 30 sample events and notes 9 are not in the sample, which is accurate (39 total - 30 sample = 9). All numeric claims are traceable.
